title: [SDK 52] Splash screen image scaled very small on development builds
body:
### Minimal reproducible example

https://github.com/expo/expo/tree/main/templates/expo-template-default

### What platform(s) does this occur on?

Android, iOS

### Where did you reproduce the issue?

in a development build

### Summary

Splash screen image is scaled very small on iOS development builds, but not Expo Go.

Using default template via `npx create-expo-app@latest --template default@beta` and run dev build via: `npx expo prebuild --clean --platform ios && npx expo run:ios`

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
Was able to get this working. If you are using Prebuild and have `ios.splash.logoWidth` in your `app.json`|`app.config.ts` file it is missing in the return from the function that reads the configuration. 
https://github.com/expo/expo/blob/bdbf16ce2f664f739ec1e3473aadf7a134919137/packages/%40expo/prebuild-config/src/plugins/unversioned/expo-splash-screen/getIosSplashConfig.ts#L32-L63
After line 37 I added:
`logoWidth: splash.logoWidth ?? 100` 
This will also update the generated `SplashScreen.storyboard`.
If you are using `splash.logoWidth`, you can add it in that return function.

Edit: Appears there were some recent updates to these files. `logoWidth` was replaced with `imageWidth`. It is still working for me after changing my `app.config.ts` to have `ios.splash.imageWidth`.

> Previously i was able to use background image with resizemode: cover Why with sdk52 is impossible to do that?

They migrated to the new Android 12+ SplashScreen API, which no longer supports full-screen images.


![Screenshot_20241113-095813~2](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5002dbab-366e-40aa-9088-1d6be597fe74)
https://expo.dev/changelog/2024/11-12-sdk-52

https://www.reddit.com/r/androiddev/comments/155r7mt/is_there_a_way_to_show_an_image_using_the_new/?rdt=62597

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/78900611/dynamic-image-in-splash-screen-api

Just my opinion here:
I think the goal is to keep the splash screen simple and brief, as the less time it shows, the better for the user—we should focus instead on optimizing the home of the app to load faster

comments.author: participant12
comments.body:
@participant10 this is due to restrictions made by android

https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/launch/splash-screen#elements

>  The window background consists of a single opaque color. If the window background is set and is a plain color, it is used by default if the attribute isn't set.

On iOS, you can still opt to use a full screen image by passing `"enableFullScreenImage_legacy": "true"` to the plugin. Unfortunately this cannot be supported on android as google have specific requirements for splashscreens

comments.author: participant19
comments.body:
I'm migrating an app from a full screen splash screen to a splash icon one in Android, following SDK 52 upgrade.

I'm trying to follow the [Android guidelines](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/launch/splash-screen#dimensions) mentioned in [SDK 52 blog post](https://expo.dev/changelog/2024/11-12-sdk-52#notable-breaking-changes) and in the comments for this issue. 

Two questions arise:
1. What dimensions should the splash icon file be, and how the icon should be displayed in it?
2. What value should I put in the new `imageWidth` property in the `expo-splash-screen` plugin config, so that this image file is scaled properly?

If you look at the current expo template assets example, the [`adaptive-icon.png`](https://github.com/expo/expo-template-default/blob/30d36e281139d95faeb6fd181248413458f3a406/assets/images/adaptive-icon.png) and [`splash-icon.png`](https://github.com/expo/expo-template-default/blob/30d36e281139d95faeb6fd181248413458f3a406/assets/images/splash-icon.png) are identical. This coincides with the note in the guidelines which says the splash icons follows the same specifications as adaptive icons.

This means if you already have one, assuming it follows the guidelines for example via the [Figma template](https://www.figma.com/community/file/1155362909441341285/expo-app-icon-splash), you can copy and paste your adaptive icon file and reference it in the `image` property. 

However, the template also [has set](https://github.com/expo/expo-template-default/blob/30d36e281139d95faeb6fd181248413458f3a406/app.json) `imageWidth` to `200` in `app.json`, instead of using the [default `100`](https://docs.expo.dev/versions/latest/sdk/splash-screen/#configuration). Which makes me assume that is the correct `imageWidth` property value for an 1024x1024 adaptive icon.

Putting everything together, the plugin config becomes:
```json5
// app.json
      [
        "expo-splash-screen",
        {
          "backgroundColor": "#494949", // Example
          "image": "./(...)/splash-icon.png", // Identical to adaptive-icon.png
          "imageWidth": 200, // Correct number for 1024x1024 icon following adaptive icon guidelines
          "ios": {
            // You may want to use regular full screen splash on iOS 
            "image": "./(...)/splash.png", // Full screen transparent splash png
            "enableFullScreenImage_legacy": true,
            "resizeMode": "contain"
          }
        }
      ]
```
Which seems to finally look correct. Or the template is wrong. I couldn't find an explanation of why the default is `100`.

One of the comments above comes to the same conclusion I believe https://github.com/expo/expo/issues/32515#issuecomment-2518767663. 

I wish I didn't have to assume these couple of things and the documentation was a bit clearer on how the assets / Figma template, expo plugin config and Android guidelines were supposed to be used together.

comments.body: For quick reference, after some research and testing, these steps worked for my use case regarding the Splash Screen Image/Icon: 1. **Image Size**: Followed the instructions provided in this link: [Android Developer - Splash Screen](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/launch/splash-screen). 2. **Exporting**: Used Adobe Illustrator to export a high-resolution `.png` file. 3. **Expo `app.json` configuration**: ```json "plugins": [ [ "expo-splash-screen", { "image": "./assets/images/splash.png", "backgroundColor": "#ffffff", "dark": { "image": "./assets/images/splash.png", "backgroundColor": "#1C1C1C" }, "imageWidth": 300 } ] ] ``` ![adobe-illustrator-export-screen](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a85c6d5e-fbd8-4a67-b5f7-552335dc8e67)

comments.author: participant12
comments.body:
Customising the splash screen is no longer possible in expo go. That is why you are seeing the app icon being used instead of your image. This was mentioned in the SDK 52 changelog https://expo.dev/changelog/2024/11-12-sdk-52. The reason it's no longer supported is because androids splashscreen api does not support controlling the splashscreen yourself. An app can only have a single splashscreen that conforms to their specs of how it should be put together. This is also why there is no full screen splashscreen on android. As expo go is a prebuilt app, it already has a splashscreen so this is why the loading view defaults to showing the app icon.

@participant21  there is no "true" size to provide. 1024x1024 is fine. We will resize it accordingly so it doesn't really matter. 200 is just a good default that we came too because it provides the best result generally but it won't work for all icons so you can adjust it to your needs. This again relates to androids requirements. Making an icon larger than this runs the risk of it being clipped when they place it on the splashscreen. These are androids specs https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/launch/splash-screen#elements. Think of it as slots. You provide a background color and icon and they place it appropriately.  

The main difference here is instead of providing a single image, your splashscreen is composed of parts. An image and a background color. This allows for proper dark mode support, scaling on different device size classes etc.

The original api was created when things were simpler. There was no dark mode, less variance in size (on ios at least) and it was a world where expo go was all that was offered. The level of customisation in native projects now far exceeds what can be provided by expo go so it makes some compromises. This should not cause problems because dev builds exist and should be the way all real world projects are developed. Expo go is simply far too limiting and is only intended as a playground environment for learning.

comments.author: participant12
comments.body: @participant31 android provide a spec that has to be followed for the [splashscreen](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/launch/splash-screen#elements) Full screen images are no longer supported. They want an icon that is no larger than 200x200 and they place it for you. We added support for accepting a vector drawables on android so you may be able to work around it by doing that https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/views/launch/splash-screen#elements.

comments.author: participant31
participant12
comments.body: @participant32 200 is the largest android will accept. Any larger, and it will clip the image. The size of your icon doesn't really matter. 1024x1024 is fine, we will scale it down. 100 is the default if no imageWidth is provided. If your icon is square, it will be clipped to a circle. You just need to play around with the `imageSize` until you are happy with the result.
